lines.tip: Three TH sounds: think, this, thing. Slow down on each.
thought + Thursday — keep the tongue between the teeth.
TH at the start of they, thanked, them, three.
Soft TH (this, the) uses your voice; hard TH (path) is just air.
thin, thread — not 'tin' or 'tread'. Feel the air.

sets.tip: Put your tongue gently BETWEEN your teeth and blow air out. Urdu/Punjabi speakers often say “sink” for “think” — the tongue must touch the teeth.
sets.title: TH: think, not sink

lines.text: We visited a village in winter.
lines.tip: visited, village, winter — V bites, W rounds.
very (V) vs well, will, win (W). Exaggerate the lip shapes.

lines.text: The vet gave vitamins twice a week.
lines.tip: vet, vitamins (V) — week (W). Keep them apart.

lines.text: Why would I worry about wires?
lines.tip: All W: round lips, no teeth. why, would, worry, wires.

lines.text: He viewed the new video twice.
lines.tip: viewed, video (V) — new (W). Slow and clear.

sets.tip: For V, bite your lower lip lightly with your top teeth and buzz. For W, round your lips like blowing out a candle — no teeth touch.
sets.title: V vs W: vest, not west

lines.text: Put the big bag on the bench.
lines.tip: put (puff) vs big, bag, bench (voice, no puff).
Peter, purple, pen — three puffs of air.
pilot, passed, paper — palm test: feel the air.

lines.text: Buy the best bread before breakfast.
lines.tip: All B: no puff, voice on. buy, best, bread, before, breakfast.
please, pick, parcel — short, sharp puffs.

sets.tip: English P at the start of a word has a puff of air (hold your palm in front of your mouth — feel it). B has no puff and uses your voice.
sets.title: P vs B: pin, not bin

lines.text: The ship left with the sheep.
lines.tip: ship (short) vs sheep (long) — the classic pair.
sit (short) vs seat (long). Smile on seat.
lives (short) vs leaves (long).

lines.text: Fill the form, feel free to ask.
lines.tip: fill (short) vs feel (long).

lines.text: It's a big deal to build this.
lines.tip: big, build (short) vs deal (long).

sets.tip: Short i (ship, sit) is quick and relaxed. Long ee (sheep, seat) is stretched with a smile. Mixing them changes the meaning!
sets.title: ship vs sheep: short i, long ee

lines.tip: PREsent (verb) vs preSENT (noun). Same letters, different music.
reCORD (verb) vs REcord (noun).

lines.text: We need to imPROVE our IMage.
lines.tip: imPROVE — stress the second syllable.
COMpany (first), comMUnicate (second).

lines.text: She deCIded to DEvelop a plan.
lines.tip: deCIded (second), DEvelop (second). Feel the beat.

sets.tip: English has a beat: one syllable in each word is louder and longer. Stressing the wrong syllable confuses listeners — practice the CAPS syllable.
sets.title: Word stress: PREsent vs preSENT

lines.tip: Polite, safe, professional. Stress: CLA-ri-fy.

lines.text: Let me double-check and get back to you.
lines.tip: Buys you time without sounding lost.

lines.text: Just to confirm, the deadline is Friday?
lines.tip: Rising tone at the end — it's a check, not a statement.

lines.text: That's a great point. Here's what I suggest.
lines.tip: Agree first, then lead. Smooth and confident.

lines.text: I'll send you a summary after this call.
lines.tip: Shows ownership. Stress: SUM-ma-ry.

sets.tip: Say these until they feel automatic. On calls, speed matters less than sounding calm and clear.
sets.title: Client-call power phrases

lines.tip: Yes/no question — let your voice RISE at the end.
WH-question — voice FALLS at the end.
Surprise rises, then the statement falls with energy.
Polite request — gentle rise, warm tone.

lines.text: I'm sure we'll finish on time.
lines.tip: Confident statement — steady fall. No uptalk.

sets.tip: Yes/no questions rise at the end (↗). WH-questions and statements fall (↘). Flat speech sounds bored — let your voice move.
sets.title: Intonation: questions that sing
